  \par\footnotesize EXP-A1: ranked by sensitivity, balanced\_accuracy, M6 is first; ranked by accuracy, M4 would be first (0.898), and the rule ranks it 5. The difference is why accuracy never ranks a model here.
  \par\footnotesize EXP-A2: ranked by sensitivity, balanced\_accuracy, M1 is first; ranked by accuracy, M3 would be first (0.878), and the rule ranks it 7. The difference is why accuracy never ranks a model here.
  \par\footnotesize EXP-A2 is nested: every outer fold ran its own reduced-budget search on inner folds of its training rows only. Median search trials per outer fold: M1 12, M3 12, M4 12, M5 5, M8 12. Write it up as that budget, never as 'tuned' unqualified.
  \par\footnotesize The shipped final binary model is M1, first in EXP-A2 by the pre-registered rule. It is not distinguishable from M6 on sensitivity (paired t-test, n=25 folds, p=0.725, Holm-corrected 1.000), so the table does not show that M1 outperforms the ensemble; it shows they are tied and M1 is simpler.
  \par\footnotesize Every PhysioNet figure here is cross-validated WITHIN the PhysioNet 2016 corpus. Holding out one recording sub-collection at a time (EXP-F3, T-S5) takes ROC-AUC from 0.922-0.942 pooled to 0.426-0.533 across the 6 models, so no number here is a claim of generalization, deployment-readiness or field performance.
  \par\footnotesize Mean and SD are over the 25 folds of the repeated 5x5 subject-grouped map (sample SD, ddof=1). Folds of a repeated CV overlap, so the SD is a spread, not a standard error; T28 carries the paired tests.
  \par\footnotesize M9 (1D-CNN) is out of scope on CPU-only hardware and was not run; no comparison against a convolutional network is made.
  \par\footnotesize PV-MEPCG / PulseVision is an academic screening and decision-support prototype, not a diagnostic tool.
